headline: OpenAI's AI pipeline found 948 Linux privilege-escalation flaws in a single $1.2M run
summary: OpenAI's new autonomous security pipeline, powered by an unnamed cyber model, discovered 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits in the Linux kernel for $1,279 per exploit. Each finding includes a candidate patch and root-cause analysis.
details: OpenAI has unveiled an autonomous vulnerability-discovery pipeline that conducted a large-scale security review of the Linux kernel. This system, powered by an upcoming cyber model, operates through four stages: discovery, dynamic validation, exploitability assessment, and patch generation. Each stage is automated, passing its output to the next without human intervention until the final review.

The pipeline identified 2,308 candidate kernel findings in a mid-October run against a stock desktop Linux distribution in an isolated environment. Of these, 1,724 were dynamically reproduced as genuine vulnerabilities, leading to 291 proofs of concept for information leaks. Ultimately, 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits were delivered, each with a candidate patch and root-cause analysis.

The economic efficiency of this run is remarkable, costing $1,213,430 in API credits. This translates to approximately $1,279 per working exploit. These figures provide security teams with a clear budget line for reproducible, documented, and patchable kernel flaws.

Despite the automation, human researchers remain crucial, reviewing every output before any report leaves the lab. This ensures that all findings are thoroughly vetted before being shared with maintainers or partners. Reporting prioritizes critical vulnerabilities, aligning with Linux kernel community guidance.

This effort significantly expands upon the June 2026 Patch the Planet initiative, where GPT-5.5 Cyber produced 24 Linux kernel local privilege-escalation exploits. The new pipeline delivered roughly forty times that output, demonstrating a substantial leap in automated vulnerability discovery.

The impact on security research is profound, transforming it into a systematic, budgeted pipeline that generates, reproduces, proves, and patches flaws before human review. For kernel maintainers, this promises increased patch velocity for long-tail flaws that previously took years to address, with candidate patches arriving through established upstream review processes.

headline: Labrinth creates a song from scratch live tonight on Apple's new MacBook Pro
summary: The Grammy-winning artist will compose a full track live overnight at Apple's Tower Theatre store, showcasing the capabilities of the new MacBook Pro.
details: Apple is hosting a special livestream event featuring Grammy-winning singer-songwriter Labrinth. The artist will compose an entire song from scratch live at Apple's Tower Theatre store.
This unique performance aims to demonstrate the creative power and performance capabilities of Apple's new MacBook Pro. Labrinth will work overnight to complete the track.
Viewers can tune in tonight to watch the creative process unfold in real-time. The event highlights how professional artists utilize Apple's hardware for music production.
